For the first PR looks good to me, please wait for another approval before merging.

I really like your security considerations which you outlined in this document. Good stuff.

One suggestion would be to consider using Access Tokens (for the web) instead of a session cookie. This way you can re-use the same code for API tokens and Access Tokens generation/verification. It also will give you CSRF protection for private endpoints (as you will be passing it in the Authorization header). There will be one public endpoint (login) which is OK because it would be a POST request (so no CSRF protection is required).

You can store AccessTokens in the localStorage on the client side.

This way you do not need to use cookies, csrf tokens, and can reuse a common code which should reduce the scope and still give a reasonable protection for this project.
LGTM on the backend pieces, wait for others to approve the frontend

Looks good to me. I would also add HTTP headers to exposed APIs for a better security (or make sure that the library that you are planning to use adds them).
